import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset not found. Please ensure 'data/cameras.csv' is in the correct directory.")
    # Create a dummy dataframe to avoid crashing the script
    data = {'brand': ['Nikon', 'Canon', 'Sony', 'Fuji', 'Leica'],
            'model_year': [2018, 2020, 2021, 2019, 2022],
            'megapixels': [24.5, 30.3, 61.0, 26.1, 47.3],
            'max_iso': [51200, 40000, 32000, 51200, 50000],
            'weight_grams': [675, 580, 665, 489, 734],
            'price_usd': [1999.99, 2299.00, 3498.00, 1699.00, 5995.00],
            'sensor_type': ['Full Frame', 'Full Frame', 'Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Full Frame'],
            'has_video_4k': [1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
            'lens_mount': ['Z', 'RF', 'E', 'X', 'L'],
            'body_type': ['Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'Rangefinder']}
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Prepare data for visualization
# Sort sensor types for a more logical legend order
sensor_order = ['Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Micro 4/3']
df['sensor_type'] = pd.Categorical(df['sensor_type'], categories=sensor_order, ordered=True)
df = df.sort_values('sensor_type')

# Set the visual style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatterplot
# This plot shows the relationship between Price and Megapixels,
# with additional dimensions for Sensor Type (color), Max ISO (size), and 4K capability (marker style).
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='max_iso',
    style='has_video_4k',
    palette='viridis_r',
    sizes=(30, 400),
    alpha=0.75,
    ax=ax,
    hue_order=sensor_order
)

# --- Customization for Clarity and Insight ---

# Set title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type, ISO, and 4K Capability', fontsize=18, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Format y-axis ticks as currency
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f'${int(y):,}')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()

# Separate legends for clarity
legend_elements = {}
for handle, label in zip(handles, labels):
    if label in ['sensor_type', 'max_iso', 'has_video_4k']:
        continue
    if label in sensor_order:
        legend_elements.setdefault('Sensor Type', []).append((handle, label))
    elif label in ['0', '1']:
        new_label = 'Has 4K' if label == '1' else 'No 4K'
        legend_elements.setdefault('Video Capability', []).append((handle, new_label))
    else: # This will be the size legend for max_iso
        legend_elements.setdefault('Max ISO', []).append((handle, label))

# Re-create the legend outside the plot
ax.get_legend().remove()
legend_y_start = 1.02
for title, items in legend_elements.items():
    handles_subset = [item[0] for item in items]
    labels_subset = [item[1] for item in items]
    
    # Customize marker size for sensor type legend for better visibility
    if title == 'Sensor Type':
        for h in handles_subset:
            h.set_sizes([80])
            
    leg = ax.legend(handles_subset, labels_subset,
                    title=title,
                    title_fontsize='13',
                    fontsize='11',
                    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, legend_y_start),
                    loc='upper left',
                    frameon=True,
                    borderpad=0.8)
    ax.add_artist(leg)
    legend_y_start -= (len(items) * 0.05 + 0.12) # Adjust vertical spacing for next legend

# Add a horizontal line for the median price to provide context
median_price = df['price_usd'].median()
ax.axhline(median_price, color='gray', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, zorder=0)
ax.text(df['megapixels'].max(), median_price, f' Median Price: ${median_price:,.0f}',
        color='gray', va='bottom', ha='right', fontsize=11, weight='bold')

# Adjust plot limits
ax.set_xlim(left=5)
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close(fig)
